introduction: The three commands built on one interface — `spec` (writes a package), `specr` (renders one) and `speca` (reports and changes its state) — name one another in their help, package doc comments and `--schema` descriptions through one shared constant. `specr`'s `next` suggests the `speca` call that claims a task or records it done whenever that call would succeed, as decided by one writability rule in `internal/specpkg` that `specr` and `speca` both call.

glossary.claim: The call `speca <spec_dir> --task N --state in_progress`, which moves a pending task to in_progress as a compare-and-set.
glossary.done call: The call `speca <spec_dir> --task N --state done`, which records an in-progress task as finished.
glossary.intent drift: An active package whose recorded IntentHash is set and whose PRD body's intent hash cannot be computed or differs from it.
glossary.ready task: A pending task whose dependencies are all done, reported as TaskInfo.ready.
glossary.render suggestion: specr's existing `next` element `{tool: specr, input: <spec_dir>, flags: [--task, M]}` naming the next unfinished task.
glossary.sibling sentence: The value of the constant cli.SiblingCommands: "spec writes a package from an idea, specr renders one, speca reports and changes its state."
glossary.speca entry: A `next` element whose tool is "speca": a claim or a done call.
glossary.unfinished task: A task whose state is neither done nor dropped.
glossary.whole render: A specr call without --task, with or without --section or --max-tokens.
glossary.writable package: A package with status draft, or with status active and no intent drift; the only packages speca's task and status writes accept.

requirements.title: One constant holds the sibling sentence
requirements.rationale: Three literal copies of one sentence would drift apart.

criteria.action: export an untyped string constant SiblingCommands whose value is exactly "spec writes a package from an idea, specr renders one, speca reports and changes its state."
criteria.contract: cli.SiblingCommands compiles in a const expression concatenated with a raw-string constant

criteria.action: hold the literal sibling sentence only in the declaration of cli.SiblingCommands, so that every non-test .go file under cmd/spec, cmd/specr and cmd/speca obtains it by referencing cli.SiblingCommands
criteria.contract: a scan of non-test .go files finds the sentence text in exactly one file, internal/cli

requirements.title: Every command's help names the other two
requirements.rationale: An agent that finds one command learns about the other two from the command itself.

criteria.condition: spec, specr or speca is invoked with -h or --help
criteria.action: print its help to stderr with a line equal to cli.SiblingCommands placed after the title line and before the `Usage:` line, with a blank line directly before it and directly after it
criteria.contract:
exit code 0; stdout is empty; stderr contains "

" + cli.SiblingCommands + "

" before the first "Usage:"

criteria.condition: spec, specr or speca is invoked with no arguments while stdout is not a terminal
criteria.action: print the same help, including the sibling line, to stderr and write a usage envelope to stdout
criteria.contract: exit code 2; stdout holds an envelope with error category usage; stderr contains cli.SiblingCommands

criteria.action: say in its output paragraph that `next` names the task to render after this one and, when the package can take the change, the speca call that claims the rendered task or records it done
criteria.contract: specr --help stderr contains "speca" within the paragraph describing next, and still contains "specr <spec> --task N"

criteria.action: carry the sibling sentence from cli.SiblingCommands in place of the literal line written by 10_speca_state_report, and contain no occurrence of the old wording "speca reports its state"
criteria.contract: speca --help stderr contains cli.SiblingCommands and does not contain "speca reports its state"

criteria.system: package doc comments of cmd/spec, cmd/specr and cmd/speca
criteria.action: each contain one sentence that names the other two commands of the three
criteria.contract: the parsed package doc of each command contains the names of both other commands within a single sentence

requirements.title: Every --schema description names the other two
requirements.rationale: A framework that declares one tool reads what it does first, then that two siblings exist.

criteria.condition: specr is invoked with --schema
criteria.action: emit a description equal to its existing description sentence followed by one space and cli.SiblingCommands
criteria.contract: exit code 0; the JSON document's description field ends with " " + cli.SiblingCommands and starts with specr's own sentence

criteria.condition: speca is invoked with --schema
criteria.action: emit a description equal to its own description sentence followed by one space and cli.SiblingCommands, replacing the literal sibling sentence written by 10_speca_state_report
criteria.contract: exit code 0; the description field ends with " " + cli.SiblingCommands and contains no other copy of a sibling sentence

criteria.action: match cmd/specr/testdata/schema.golden.json and cmd/speca/testdata/schema.golden.json byte for byte against the regenerated --schema output, with the description value as the only change: no flag, result field or exit code is added, removed or altered
criteria.contract: TestSchemaGolden passes for both commands without UPDATE_GOLDEN set; the flags, result and exit_codes members equal those before this change

requirements.title: One answer to whether a package can take a write
requirements.rationale: specr and speca must agree on writability, and a rule written twice drifts.

criteria.action: return true exactly when spec.Status is active, spec.IntentHash is non-nil, and afspec.ComputeIntentHash(spec.PRDBody) either returns an error or returns a hash different from *spec.IntentHash
criteria.contract: bool result; false for draft, sealed, superseded or archived packages and for an active package with no IntentHash

criteria.action: for any spec with status in {draft, active, sealed, superseded, archived}, IntentHash set or unset, and a PRD body that matches, mismatches or lacks `## Intent`, return exactly (status == draft) || (status == active && !IntentDrift(spec))
criteria.contract: bool result equal to the formula for every generated combination

criteria.condition: IntentDrift or Writable is called with a nil spec
criteria.action: return false without dereferencing the spec
criteria.contract: both functions return false; no panic

criteria.action: decide intent drift and writability for the report's intent_drift, the task form's status refusal and the report's and list's claim suggestions only by calling specpkg.IntentDrift and specpkg.Writable, with no private drift helper left in cmd/speca
criteria.contract: speca's envelopes for report, list and task forms are unchanged from before this change; cmd/speca declares no function computing intent drift

criteria.condition: specr has loaded a package
criteria.action: call specpkg.Writable once for that call and keep the answer in an unexported field of its Result
criteria.contract: the specr JSON result and the --schema result description contain no writable or intent_drift key

requirements.title: specr's next after a whole render
requirements.rationale: After a whole render, the claim follows speca's report rule so the two commands never suggest different claims.

criteria.condition: specr completes a whole render
criteria.guard: the package is writable, no task is in_progress, and the first unfinished task M in plan order is pending and ready
criteria.action: add to next the entry {tool: "speca", input: result.spec_dir, flags: ["--task", "M", "--state", "in_progress"]}
criteria.contract: next[0] is the claim of M and next[1] is the render suggestion naming M

criteria.condition: specr adds a claim entry after a whole render
criteria.action: set the entry's why to name task M and its title, state that it is the next ready task, and state that it is to be claimed before working on it so that no other agent takes it
criteria.contract: why contains the task id, the task title and the word "claim"

criteria.condition: after a whole render any task in the plan is in_progress
criteria.action: add no speca entry to next
criteria.contract: next holds no element with tool "speca"; the render suggestion is unchanged

criteria.condition: after a whole render the first unfinished task is not ready
criteria.action: add no speca entry to next
criteria.contract: next holds no element with tool "speca"

criteria.condition: after a whole render the package is not writable (sealed, superseded, archived, or active with intent drift)
criteria.action: add no speca entry to next
criteria.contract: next holds no element with tool "speca"

criteria.condition: after a whole render no unfinished task remains in the plan
criteria.action: produce no next entries
criteria.contract: next is empty or absent in the envelope

criteria.action: for any package state (status, intent hash, task states and dependencies), hold a claim in specr's whole-render next exactly when `speca <spec>`'s report next holds a claim, with both naming the same task, and that task equal to the one named by specr's render suggestion
criteria.contract: the claim entries of both envelopes are equal element by element, or both absent

requirements.title: specr's next after a task render
requirements.rationale: An explicit --task is the caller's choice; the claim or done call is suggested only where it would succeed.

criteria.condition: specr completes a task render of task N
criteria.guard: the package is writable and N is pending and ready
criteria.action: add to next {tool: "speca", input: result.spec_dir, flags: ["--task", "N", "--state", "in_progress"]} with a why saying to claim task N before working on it, whether or not another task is in_progress
criteria.contract: next[0] is the claim of N

criteria.condition: specr completes a task render of task N
criteria.guard: the package is writable and N is in_progress
criteria.action: add to next {tool: "speca", input: result.spec_dir, flags: ["--task", "N", "--state", "done"]} with a why saying to record task N done once its work is finished and its tests pass
criteria.contract: next[0] is the done call of N

criteria.condition: specr renders task N while N is pending and not ready
criteria.action: add no speca entry to next
criteria.contract: next holds no element with tool "speca"

criteria.condition: specr renders task N while N is done or dropped
criteria.action: add no speca entry to next
criteria.contract: next holds no element with tool "speca"

criteria.condition: specr renders task N of a package that is not writable (sealed, superseded, archived, or active with intent drift)
criteria.action: add no speca entry to next for any state of N
criteria.contract: next holds no element with tool "speca"

requirements.title: Shape and order of specr's next
requirements.rationale: next lists calls in the order an agent makes them, and programs filtering next by tool see no change to the render suggestion.

criteria.condition: specr's next holds a speca entry
criteria.guard: a render suggestion is also present
criteria.action: place the speca entry first and the render suggestion second
criteria.contract: len(next) == 2; next[0].tool == "speca"; next[1].tool == "specr"

criteria.action: keep the render suggestion's selection rule, flags and why identical to those before this change, and when no render suggestion exists emit only the speca entry or nothing
criteria.contract: the specr element of next equals the pre-change element for the same package and flags

criteria.action: set each speca entry's input to result.spec_dir and its flags to four separate elements: "--task", the task id, "--state", and the target state
criteria.contract: speca entry input equals the render suggestion's input; len(flags) == 4

criteria.condition: specr fails to write its --markdown-file after rendering
criteria.action: still emit next, including any speca entry, by the same rules from Result.Next()
criteria.contract: exit code 1; the envelope holds result and next with the same entries as a successful render of the same package

criteria.condition: specr cannot load the package
criteria.action: emit no next entries
criteria.contract: exit code 1; the envelope has an error and no next

criteria.action: leave every file of the package unchanged on disk for any render, including those whose next holds a speca entry
criteria.contract: tasks.json and the other package files are byte-identical before and after the call

execution_paths.title: An agent renders a package, claims the suggested task with speca, and the plan records it in progress

steps.action: runs `specr <spec>` on a draft package with no task in progress and task 1 pending and ready
loads the package, calls specpkg.Writable, renders the Markdown and emits next = [speca claim of task 1, specr --task 1]
checks specpkg.Writable, accepts the claim and saves tasks.json with task 1 in_progress

execution_paths.title: An agent renders its in-progress task and records it done through speca

steps.action: runs `specr <spec> --task 1` on a writable package where task 1 is in_progress
renders the package scoped to task 1 and emits next with `speca <spec_dir> --task 1 --state done` first and `specr <spec_dir> --task 2` second
accepts the transition and saves tasks.json with task 1 done

execution_paths.title: A reader of any command's help or schema learns of the other two

steps.action: writes its help to stderr with the cli.SiblingCommands line before `Usage:`, or its schema document to stdout with a description ending in cli.SiblingCommands, and exits 0
